Revenue is built in USD by vertical (usdBuild), converted at the stated INR/USD path; revenueGrowth below is that build expressed in rupees (checked in tools/authoring/TECHM.ctx.js). Margins are set on the company's EBIT definition; the engine's EBITDA margin = EBIT margin + depreciation as a % of revenue (the engine's own depreciation). usdBuild._why: FY27: Q1 USD 1,660 mn (+6.1% YoY reported, +6.6% CC, organic +6.2%); Q2 loses 1-1.3% from the European auto programme delivered early in Q1, offset by a large telecom deal that had not started ramping and the end of a cloud pass-through drag; we assume ~+1% QoQ in Q2 and ~1.5% in Q3-Q4, i.e. FY27 USD 6,772 mn (+6.1%), in line with brokers (USD 6,745-6,792 mn). By vertical: communications +3.5% (Q1 +1.3% YoY; deal ramp vs 'volatility in a large US telecoms client'), manufacturing +12% (Q1 +17.2%, aerospace, auto pull-forward), BFSI +9% (Q1 +8.1% plus the Avant acquisition), TME +2% (volatile client spend), retail/logistics +8%, healthcare +7%. FY28-29: +5% a year, below the street's 5-7.5% for FY28: once the large-deal ramps are in the base, Tech Mahindra faces the same AI deflation as peers (HCLTech: legacy revenue erosion of 2-3% a year; peers guide 1-4% CC for FY27). Constant-currency growth assumed equal to reported after FY27 (no cross-currency view).
usdBuild._fxWhy: INR/USD averaged 89.0 in FY26, 94.6 in Q1FY27 and closed 95.81-95.83 on 30-Sep-2026. Forecasts published by then: BMI 97 by Mar-2027 and 99 by Mar-2028; Axis Bank 97 by Dec-2026 and 100 by Jun-2027. We use 95.5 / 97.0 / 98.5 (about 1.5% depreciation a year), the cautious end of those forecasts.

assumptions._revWhy: INR revenue = USD build x INR/USD path: Rs64,671 cr (FY27E), Rs68,977 cr (FY28E), Rs73,559 cr (FY29E). FY27's 13.8% rupee growth is 6.1% in dollars plus 7.3% from the weaker rupee (89.0 to 95.5).
assumptions._marginWhy: EBIT (company definition) 6.1% (FY24), 9.7% (FY25), 12.6% (FY26), 14.4% in Q1FY27 after 11 straight quarters of expansion; management targets 15% for FY27 and says Q4FY27 'has to be upwards of 15%'. Q2 carries phased wage hikes and the auto reversal, so FY27E 14.8% (Q1 14.4, ~14.3 Q2, ~15.0 Q3, ~15.4 Q4), within the street's 14.6-15.1%. FY28E 15.3% and FY29E 15.6%: a weaker rupee (+1.5% a year) and fixed-price productivity help, but the onsite-heavy large deals, AI investment and productivity pass-backs in renewals cap the gain; management has not set a target beyond FY27. Street FY28E 14.8-15.9%. The engine needs EBITDA margin: EBIT margin + depreciation (engine) of Rs1,962 / 2,015 / 2,071 cr = 3.03% / 2.92% / 2.82% of revenue.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex Rs1,015 cr (FY23), Rs791 cr (FY24), Rs594 cr (FY25), Rs696 cr (FY26): ~1.1-1.3% of revenue for an asset-light services firm (offices, computers, software). Rs850-950 cr (~1.3% of revenue) allows for the new experience centres in Pune and Hyderabad mentioned on the Q1FY27 call. Leased offices (right-of-use assets) are outside capex.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation and amortisation Rs1,882 cr = 6.2% of average gross block (Rs30,426 cr, incl. intangibles and right-of-use assets); Q1FY27 Rs479 cr (Rs1,916 cr annualised). The engine grows gross block only with capex (lease additions are not modelled), so 6.1% gives Rs1,962 cr in FY27E, close to the run-rate.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied by the engine to net treasury (cash Rs5,105 cr + investments Rs3,426 cr - borrowings incl. leases Rs2,186 cr = Rs6,345 cr at Mar-26). FY26 treasury income (interest Rs98 cr + gains on FVTPL investments Rs154 cr + dividends Rs0.3 cr = Rs252 cr; AR FY26 note 29) was 3.1% of average gross cash and investments (~Rs8,000 cr, much of it held abroad at low rates) and 4.2% of average net treasury (Rs6,022 cr). 4.0% on net treasury = Rs254 cr in FY27E.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income = miscellaneous and rental income less FX losses. Misc + rental: Rs252 cr in FY26 (misc Rs234 cr incl. fair-value changes of acquisition obligations, rental Rs18 cr), Rs311 cr in FY25; we use Rs190 / 200 / 210 cr. FX (hedge and translation) losses: -USD 52 mn in FY26 (Rs480 cr), -USD 23 mn (~Rs218 cr) in Q1FY27 as the rupee fell from 85.3 to 94.6. The hedge book shrank from USD 1.96 bn (Mar-25) to USD 0.72 bn (Jun-26) with tenor cut to one year, so most hedges written before the fall have matured; Q2FY27 still carries a ~1.4% rupee fall. FX: -Rs400 cr (FY27E: Q1 actual -218, ~-80 in Q2, ~-50 a quarter in H2), -Rs100 cr (FY28E), -Rs50 cr (FY29E). Total other income FY27E ~Rs44 cr vs Rs32 cr in FY26 and -Rs292 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 (ex the Rs272 cr Labour Code charge); the gap to the TTM is the FX line (TTM -Rs720 cr). Ex-FX, FY27E (Rs444 cr) equals Q1FY27 annualised (Rs111 cr x 4) and is below FY26 (Rs510 cr).
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance costs (mainly interest on lease liabilities)
assumptions._interestWhy: Rs326 cr (FY23), Rs392 cr (FY24), Rs322 cr (FY25), Rs337 cr (FY26); Q1FY27 Rs111 cr as lease liabilities rose to Rs2,117 cr (Mar-26) from Rs1,554 cr. Borrowings excluding leases are only ~Rs70 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (no minority line in the engine). FY26 effective tax 27% (24.3% in Q4); management: FY27 'in a similar range'. Q1FY27: tax Rs556 cr + minorities Rs21 cr on PBT Rs2,042 cr = 28.2%. Minorities are partners in Comviva and other subsidiaries.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Policy: at least 85% of free cash flow over five years as dividends and/or buybacks. FY26: Rs51 a share (interim 15 + final 36) = 94% of basic EPS and 91% of FCF; FY25 Rs45 = 94%. FCF has run at 100-115% of PAT, so 85% of EPS is the policy floor, not a forecast of cuts.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash, but a mid-tier IT exporter with a volatile earnings history (FY24 EPS halved) and heavy telecom exposure: beta 1.0, Ke 12.5%.
dcf._tgWhy: Rupee revenue growth of 5% after FY38 = ~2-3% dollar growth (AI deflation eats part of volume) plus ~2% rupee depreciation; the low end of the house 5-6% range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Rupee revenue growth fades from 6.6% (FY29E) to 5% over twelve years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin ~18.4% in FY29E (EBIT 15.6%) eases to 18%: pricing pressure from AI pass-backs offsets further productivity; Tech Mahindra has never sustained an EBIT margin above ~15%.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Large-deal ramps and above-peer growth persist (USD ~7% a year in FY28-29), AI work grows faster than legacy work shrinks, and the margin keeps rising to ~16.5% by FY29 on pyramid and rupee tailwinds; the sector partly re-rates.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: AI deflation reaches Tech Mahindra's run contracts and communications clients (USD growth ~2% a year after FY27), the 15% margin is missed as pricing gives back productivity, and the stock trades like the de-rated Tier-1 peers.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Tech Mahindra: every broker that discloses a method uses P/E on FY28E or Jun-28E EPS (16.9-20x; Jul-Sep 2026). 16x = the stock's 23.3x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 on reported EPS (house trough rule: FY24 left out; 26.0x with it, 21.2x if FY25 is also left out, 23.8x on EPS before the FY25-26 one-offs) cut by the 31.3% median de-rating of the nine-stock IT peer set versus each stock's five-year median P/E at 30-Sep-2026 (TCS -53%, Infosys -49%, Wipro -40%, LTIMindtree -38%, LTTS -31%, Mphasis -27%, HCLTech -21%, Persistent -18%, Coforge -11%) = 16.0x. No further growth or returns adjustment (a justified P/E at our 12.5% cost of equity, 6.5% growth and 85% payout is 15.1x, so returns do not argue for more). Bull 18x (the stock's FY28E multiple today; Elara and Nomura). Bear 13x (the incumbents-only de-rating of -44.5% applied to 23.3x = 12.9x; Infosys and Wipro trade at 12-13x).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value. 9x Sep-28E EBITDA = the stock's 12.7x median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (FY24 left out; EV on the 88.6 cr shares outside the TML Benefit Trust) less the same 31.3% sector de-rating = 8.7x. Bull 10x (today's forward multiple), bear 7x (incumbents-only de-rating).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 12-year FCFF at Ke 12.5%, terminal growth 5%, plus net cash.

cover.headline: The turnaround worked, and the price already knows it: a de-rated sector does not pay 18x for a mid-tier IT firm
cover.lead: Tech Mahindra, the Mahindra group's USD 6.4 bn IT services company, has delivered almost exactly what CEO Mohit Joshi promised in April 2024: EBIT margin from 6.1% (FY24) to 14.4% in Q1FY27, dollar growth back to 6.6% in constant currency (peers guide 1-4%), USD 4.1 bn of deals in twelve months and 85%+ of free cash flow paid out. The stock held up while Indian IT had its worst year since 2008 on fears that AI agents shrink the work. We forecast EPS of ₹74.5 (FY27E) and ₹85.2 (FY28E), in line with consensus. The street values Tech Mahindra on **P/E on FY28E EPS (16.9-20x)**. Applying **16x to Sep-28E EPS of ₹89.4** (its 23.3x median forward P/E since 2021, cut by the IT sector's 31% de-rating) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹1,436, DCF ₹1,517. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: EBIT margin up for 11 straight quarters to 14.4%; Q4FY27 "upwards of 15%". Q1FY27 revenue +6.1% YoY in dollars with every vertical growing, ROCE 28.3%, FCF 108% of profit. Management credibility is the best it has been in a decade.

arguments.h: But FY27 is the easy year
arguments.p: Growth comes off a flat FY24-26 base, large-deal ramps and an auto programme pulled into Q1 (a 1-1.3% Q2 headwind). Communications (32%) grew only 1.3% with "volatility in a large US telecoms client". Margin levers (utilisation 87%, subcontractors, SG&A) are largely used, and there is no plan beyond FY27.

arguments.h: AI is a sector problem, not a cycle
arguments.p: HCLTech says deals are ~20% smaller for the same scope; Cognizant passes AI savings to clients; Gartner cut IT-services growth to 5.3%. Tech Mahindra's mix (BPS 16%, testing, infrastructure operations, telecom run work) is more exposed than most. We expect the sector's lower multiples to last.

arguments.h: Valuation: the premium is the risk
arguments.p: At ₹1,524 the stock trades at 20.5x FY27E and 17.9x FY28E EPS, a 20-35% premium to Tier-1 peers that have de-rated by 40-50%. On the sector's de-rating our 16x gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}. The DCF (₹1,517) says the price is fair only if today's growth and margins hold for a decade.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): growth after the European auto reversal, the margin hit from phased wage hikes, and whether the large telecom deal starts ramping.
FY27 delivery: the 15% EBIT margin and above-peer growth; ROCE above 30% by Q4FY27.
A roadmap beyond FY27 (margin and growth goals for FY28-30), likely with the Q4FY27 results.
Sector: peers' guidance (Infosys, HCLTech), AI-deflation evidence in renewals, US policy (H-1B fee, proposed HIRE Act).
Rupee: a faster fall lifts EBIT but brings back hedge losses; the hedge book is down to USD 0.72 bn.

sections.title: A USD 6.4 bn IT services firm built around telecom, now selling itself as a vertical specialist

blocks.p: Tech Mahindra sells IT and business-process work to large companies, mostly in the US and Europe. **IT services** (application development and maintenance, enterprise packages such as SAP and Salesforce, cloud and infrastructure management, engineering services, network services for telecom operators, data and AI) were ₹47,767 cr or 84% of FY26 revenue; **BPS** (customer support, back-office and AI-operations work; ~64,000 people) ₹9,048 cr or 16%. It is part of the Mahindra group (M&M owns 25.3%) and grew out of a 1980s joint venture with British Telecom, which is why **communications is still a third of revenue**, far more than at any large Indian peer. Two portfolio companies have their own products: Comviva (telecom and fintech software, seasonal, strongest in Q4) and Pininfarina (Italian car and architecture design).

FY26 revenue was USD 6,385 mn (₹56,815 cr) from ~1,100 active clients; 29 clients paid more than USD 50 mn a year (33 by Jun-2026) and the top 10 were 24% of revenue. It employed 1,46,760 people at Jun-2026 (IT 74,689, BPS 64,080), 77.5% of IT staff offshore in India. Revenue per head is low against peers because BPS is a large, low-price business.

sections.title: The central question: is the 2026 IT de-rating a cycle or AI shrinking the work? Mostly AI, we think

blocks.p: Indian IT stocks had their worst year since 2008 in 2026. The trigger was AI: Anthropic's Claude Cowork plug-ins (late Jan-2026) and its post on modernising COBOL with Claude Code (24-Feb) caused the Nifty IT index's worst days since 2020, on the fear that agents will do much of the coding, testing and support work that Indian firms bill by the hour. By 30-Sep-2026 the index was ~28% down for the year against 13% for the Nifty 50, and the five largest IT firms had lost almost half their combined value since Aug-2024. Trailing P/E multiples fell to 13.8x (TCS), 12.9x (Infosys), 11.9x (Wipro) and 18.4x (HCLTech), 31% below their five-year medians (median of nine IT peers). Tech Mahindra fell least (12% in Jan-Feb against 16-24% for peers) because its own earnings are rising.

blocks.callout: **Our answer: mostly structural, with a cyclical layer on top.** The cyclical part is real: US tariffs, the Iran war and oil at ~USD 100, weak discretionary spending and foreign selling of Indian equities (the Nifty 50 is down too). But the strongest evidence comes from the companies themselves: HCLTech says deals are ~20% smaller for the same scope and legacy revenue erodes 2-3% a year; Cognizant passes AI productivity to clients; Accenture says budgets are flat; Gartner cut its IT-services growth forecast while total tech spending accelerated; TCS, Infosys and HCLTech all shrank headcount. Record deal wins (TCS USD 9.5 bn, HCLTech USD 2.4 bn net new, Tech Mahindra USD 1.1 bn) are not turning into revenue growth at the same pace: that gap is what deflation looks like. We therefore treat the de-rating as mostly lasting: a return to the 22-30x multiples of 2021-24 needs growth of 7-8% that no large firm is guiding for. The upside for investors is earnings growth, not a re-rating.

sections.title: Does Tech Mahindra escape the sector's problem? For FY27 yes; after that, probably not

blocks.p: Tech Mahindra grew +6.6% YoY in constant currency in Q1FY27 (organic +6.2%) while Infosys cut its FY27 guidance to 1.5-3%, HCLTech guides 1-4%, TCS was flat sequentially and Wipro shrank. That gap has three sources, and only one of them is durable. (1) **Its own recovery:** FY24-26 revenue was flat, so the comparison base is low and the large deals signed in FY26 (USD 3.8 bn, +42%) are now ramping. (2) **One-offs:** a European auto programme delivered early added 1-1.3% to Q1 and reverses in Q2. (3) **Mix:** telecom, aerospace and BFSI sub-segments where it built domain depth are growing. Against that, communications (32% of revenue) grew only 1.3% and management flags "volatility in a large US telecoms client".

blocks.p: Tech Mahindra won USD 1,078 mn of new deals in Q1FY27, its third straight USD 1 bn+ quarter (USD 4,063 mn over twelve months, +37.5%). Clients paying over USD 50 mn rose from 26 to 33 in a year. At the same time IT headcount fell to 74,689 (−7% YoY): management says AI tools lifted productivity on its large fixed-price portfolio, so leavers were not replaced. IT revenue per IT employee rose from ~USD 69,000 in FY26 to ~USD 75,000 (Q1FY27 annualised). Utilisation is a high 87.0%, attrition 11.8%. Wage hikes start in Q2FY27, phased. blocks.p: Project Fortius took the company EBIT margin from 6.1% (FY24) to 12.6% (FY26) and 14.4% in Q1FY27. The Analyst Day bridge (Apr-2026) lists the levers: offshoring, fixed-price productivity, rotating staff to cheaper grades (N-1), cutting subcontractors, G&A savings, pricing, and FX tailwinds, against wage hikes and investments. Compensation fell to 64.4% of revenue in FY26 (−250 bp). In Q1FY27 the gain came from SG&A (portfolio-company back offices merged) while gross margin was hit by visa costs, Comviva seasonality and the low-margin auto acceleration. Q2 brings wage hikes and the auto reversal; management says Q4FY27 "has to be upwards of 15%" and that it will "hit" 15% for the year, but has set no path beyond FY27.

sections.title: Ten years of revenue growth, five years of flat earnings: EPS was ₹51 in FY21 and ₹54 in FY26

blocks.p: Tech Mahindra's revenue grew from ₹26,494 cr in FY16 to ₹56,815 cr in FY26, about 7.9% a year in rupees, but profit attributable to shareholders only from ₹2,993 cr to ₹4,811 cr (4.9% a year). The last five years were a round trip. Revenue jumped 18% in FY22 and 19% in FY23 on a post-Covid boom and acquisitions (~₹4,600 cr of non-treasury investing outflows in FY22 alone), then fell 2% in FY24 when telecom and hi-tech clients cut spending. The EBITDA margin halved from 18% (FY21-22) to 8.7% (FY24) and EPS fell from ₹63.4 (FY22) to ₹26.7 (FY24). The turnaround since then is real: margin 13.1% in FY25 and 15.9% in FY26, EPS back to ₹54.3. But FY26 EPS is still below FY22, and in dollars revenue was flat for three years (USD 6,277 mn in FY24, 6,264 mn in FY25, 6,385 mn in FY26).

bullets: **Cash backs profit.** Cash from operations was 128% of attributable profit in FY26, 136% in FY25 and 270% in FY24; company free cash flow was 115% of PAT in FY26 and 108% in Q1FY27. Over FY15-26 operating cash (₹59,285 cr) exceeded profit (₹46,811 cr).

**Unbilled revenue is large.** ₹5,821 cr of the ₹13,358 cr of receivables at Mar-2026 was unbilled (work done, not yet invoiced), typical of fixed-price contracts but a judgement area; DSO 84-95 days is long against Tier-1 peers.

**Goodwill and acquired intangibles** of ₹10,426 cr (35% of net worth) come mostly from acquisitions; impairment testing is a key audit matter. Small impairments (₹27 cr in FY25) and liquidations of failed units show some buys did not work.
**One-offs in history:** a ₹450 cr property-sale gain (FY25) and a ₹272 cr Labour Code charge (FY26). We show our P/E history on both reported EPS and EPS before them.

**Two EPS figures circulate.** Reported basic EPS (FY26 ₹54.28) excludes the 9.42 cr treasury shares held by the TML Benefit Trust; Screener divides by all ~98 cr issued shares (₹49.10). We use the reported basis, as the company and brokers do.

**Contingent liabilities** are material: income-tax disputes ₹985 cr (mostly transfer pricing), a ₹1,275 cr service-tax demand on onsite services (2008-13) before the Supreme Court, and ₹624 cr of other claims not acknowledged.

**Satyam legacy:** ₹1,230 cr of "alleged advances" claimed by 37 companies from the old Satyam sits in a suspense account outside equity and liabilities by court order; the auditor (B S R & Co.) has repeated an emphasis of matter on it every year. Management expects nothing to be payable.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER (mild).** Unmodified audit opinion, cash conversion above 100% and transparent disclosure of FX and exceptional items. We stop short of green because of the size of goodwill and unbilled revenue, the earn-out fair-value gains that pass through other income, the long-running Satyam emphasis of matter and ₹2,900 cr of tax and other contingent claims (~10% of net worth).

FY28E 15.3% and FY29E 15.6%: a weaker rupee (+1.5% a year) and fixed-price productivity help, but the onsite-heavy large deals, AI investment and productivity pass-backs in renewals cap the gain; management has not set a target beyond FY27. assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex Rs1,015 cr (FY23), Rs791 cr (FY24), Rs594 cr (FY25), Rs696 cr (FY26): ~1.1-1.3% of revenue for an asset-light services firm (offices, computers, software). Rs850-950 cr (~1.3% of revenue) allows for the new experience centres in Pune and Hyderabad mentioned on the Q1FY27 call. Leased offices (right-of-use assets) are outside capex.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation and amortisation Rs1,882 cr = 6.2% of average gross block (Rs30,426 cr, incl. intangibles and right-of-use assets); Q1FY27 Rs479 cr (Rs1,916 cr annualised). The engine grows gross block only with capex (lease additions are not modelled), so 6.1% gives Rs1,962 cr in FY27E, close to the run-rate.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied by the engine to net treasury (cash Rs5,105 cr + investments Rs3,426 cr - borrowings incl. leases Rs2,186 cr = Rs6,345 cr at Mar-26). FY26 treasury income (interest Rs98 cr + gains on FVTPL investments Rs154 cr + dividends Rs0.3 cr = Rs252 cr; AR FY26 note 29) was 3.1% of average gross cash and investments (~Rs8,000 cr, much of it held abroad at low rates) and 4.2% of average net treasury (Rs6,022 cr). 4.0% on net treasury = Rs254 cr in FY27E.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income = miscellaneous and rental income less FX losses. Misc + rental: Rs252 cr in FY26 (misc Rs234 cr incl. fair-value changes of acquisition obligations, rental Rs18 cr), Rs311 cr in FY25; we use Rs190 / 200 / 210 cr. FX (hedge and translation) losses: -USD 52 mn in FY26 (Rs480 cr), -USD 23 mn (~Rs218 cr) in Q1FY27 as the rupee fell from 85.3 to 94.6. The hedge book shrank from USD 1.96 bn (Mar-25) to USD 0.72 bn (Jun-26) with tenor cut to one year, so most hedges written before the fall have matured; Q2FY27 still carries a ~1.4% rupee fall. FX: -Rs400 cr (FY27E: Q1 actual -218, ~-80 in Q2, ~-50 a quarter in H2), -Rs100 cr (FY28E), -Rs50 cr (FY29E). Total other income FY27E ~Rs44 cr vs Rs32 cr in FY26 and -Rs292 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 (ex the Rs272 cr Labour Code charge); the gap to the TTM is the FX line (TTM -Rs720 cr). Ex-FX, FY27E (Rs444 cr) equals Q1FY27 annualised (Rs111 cr x 4) and is below FY26 (Rs510 cr).
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance costs (mainly interest on lease liabilities)
assumptions._interestWhy: Rs326 cr (FY23), Rs392 cr (FY24), Rs322 cr (FY25), Rs337 cr (FY26); Q1FY27 Rs111 cr as lease liabilities rose to Rs2,117 cr (Mar-26) from Rs1,554 cr. Borrowings excluding leases are only ~Rs70 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (no minority line in the engine). FY26 effective tax 27% (24.3% in Q4); management: FY27 'in a similar range'. Q1FY27: tax Rs556 cr + minorities Rs21 cr on PBT Rs2,042 cr = 28.2%. Minorities are partners in Comviva and other subsidiaries.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Policy: at least 85% of free cash flow over five years as dividends and/or buybacks. FY26: Rs51 a share (interim 15 + final 36) = 94% of basic EPS and 91% of FCF; FY25 Rs45 = 94%. FCF has run at 100-115% of PAT, so 85% of EPS is the policy floor, not a forecast of cuts.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash, but a mid-tier IT exporter with a volatile earnings history (FY24 EPS halved) and heavy telecom exposure: beta 1.0, Ke 12.5%.
dcf._tgWhy: Rupee revenue growth of 5% after FY38 = ~2-3% dollar growth (AI deflation eats part of volume) plus ~2% rupee depreciation; the low end of the house 5-6% range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Rupee revenue growth fades from 6.6% (FY29E) to 5% over twelve years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin ~18.4% in FY29E (EBIT 15.6%) eases to 18%: pricing pressure from AI pass-backs offsets further productivity; Tech Mahindra has never sustained an EBIT margin above ~15%.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Large-deal ramps and above-peer growth persist (USD ~7% a year in FY28-29), AI work grows faster than legacy work shrinks, and the margin keeps rising to ~16.5% by FY29 on pyramid and rupee tailwinds; the sector partly re-rates.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: AI deflation reaches Tech Mahindra's run contracts and communications clients (USD growth ~2% a year after FY27), the 15% margin is missed as pricing gives back productivity, and the stock trades like the de-rated Tier-1 peers.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Tech Mahindra: every broker that discloses a method uses P/E on FY28E or Jun-28E EPS (16.9-20x; Jul-Sep 2026). 16x = the stock's 23.3x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 on reported EPS (house trough rule: FY24 left out; 26.0x with it, 21.2x if FY25 is also left out, 23.8x on EPS before the FY25-26 one-offs) cut by the 31.3% median de-rating of the nine-stock IT peer set versus each stock's five-year median P/E at 30-Sep-2026 (TCS -53%, Infosys -49%, Wipro -40%, LTIMindtree -38%, LTTS -31%, Mphasis -27%, HCLTech -21%, Persistent -18%, Coforge -11%) = 16.0x. No further growth or returns adjustment (a justified P/E at our 12.5% cost of equity, 6.5% growth and 85% payout is 15.1x, so returns do not argue for more). Bull 18x (the stock's FY28E multiple today; Elara and Nomura). Bear 13x (the incumbents-only de-rating of -44.5% applied to 23.3x = 12.9x; Infosys and Wipro trade at 12-13x).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value. 9x Sep-28E EBITDA = the stock's 12.7x median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (FY24 left out; EV on the 88.6 cr shares outside the TML Benefit Trust) less the same 31.3% sector de-rating = 8.7x. Bull 10x (today's forward multiple), bear 7x (incumbents-only de-rating).
